# WrapTextMeasure waits a fixed 50 ms for later passes and flakes under CI load

## Context

On the outside contributor's docs-only PR #21045, the `unit` job failed (run 43750807532, job 132924147387): 7,373 passed, 1 flaky, 3 skipped, exit code 1. The flaky test was `test/playwright/unit/grid/WrapTextMeasure.spec.mjs` › "a reply for a cell whose width changed in the meantime is dropped": `Expected: 85, Received: 65`. It passed on retry, but a flaky test fails the job, so an unrelated contributor PR showed a red check. Captured as defect-note c16b7923; its first mechanism was a guess, corrected in 8fdc9c42 after reading the test.

## The Problem

The arm releases a held measurement pass, then `await grid.timeout(50)`, then asserts two things: the held pass applied record 104's 65 px (its 3-line name only), and a later pass measured its note at the new width (85 px). The failing assertion is the second one. The fence held; the later pass simply had not landed within 50 ms on a loaded runner.

The spec has 20 fixed waits across its 25 tests (`grid.timeout(50)` and siblings). Two kinds are mixed:
- **Presence waits:** wait until a pass has landed, then assert its result. A fixed time makes these flaky under load.
- **Absence waits:** prove that nothing happens within a window (a dropped reply, an unchanged height). These need a fixed window and stay.

## The Architectural Reality

- Measurement runs in `View#measureRowHeights` (`src/grid/View.mjs`): a batched `getLayoutRect` read, a fence that drops replies for recycled slots, changed content or changed widths, then `View#setRowHeights`.
- The spec stubs the read (`respond`), so a test controls when replies resolve; the later pass's timing still depends on the update cycle.
- Origin of the spec: #19662 and #19692 (content-sized rows).

## The Fix

In `test/playwright/unit/grid/WrapTextMeasure.spec.mjs` only: every presence wait becomes an `expect.poll` (or `toPass`) on the observable the test asserts next, such as `view.rowGeometry.heightAt(n)` or the entries `setRowHeights` applied. Absence waits keep their fixed window, and each gets a short comment saying it proves an absence. No engine change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: No presence assertion in the spec follows a fixed wait; the remaining fixed waits each guard an absence and say so.
- [ ] AC-2: The width-change arm still fails with the fence removed (local mutation of `View#measureRowHeights`, reverted); the receipt is in the PR.
- [ ] AC-3: The spec passes `--repeat-each=10` locally while another unit run loads the machine; the receipt is in the PR.

## Out of Scope

- Playwright's policy that a flaky test fails the job.
- Fixed waits in other specs.
